newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Thousands denounce government in southern Albania.
newsitem.headline: Thousands denounce government in southern Albania.

text.p: About 3,000 depositors demanding the return of money invested in bankrupt pyramid investment schemes marched through the Albanian port of Vlore on Wednesday.

The marchers shouted slogans denouncing President Sali Berisha and his rightist government as they advanced to the city's main square. Riot police were moving alongside the marchers, but made no attempt to stop them.

"Down with the government, down with Sali Berisha!" the demonstrators shouted. Marchers demanded the government's resignation and said they would occupy the square until they were given back their money.

Investors in Europe's poorest country have already begun receiving partial refunds of their stakes in two of five failed schemes. But the refunds were marked by confusion and many people were turned away from payout points.

Banks were issuing refunds in the capital Tirana, where there was no indication of tension. Enraged depositors set fire to public buildings last month in a number of Albanian towns, particularly in the more volatile south of the Balkan country.
But a police crackdown and the threat of long jail terms on public order offences had kept many would-be protesters away from planned demonstrations last weekend.
